diagram_math_checks.objects: For fixed i,k,h, a and alpha are real n-vectors; each V_{k,h}(y_j^{(k-1)}) and b_{i,k,h} is in R^d.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition paragraph at line 27 defines the real scores and the maps V:R^d→R^d; displayed update at line 30 gives the weighted sum.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The soft branch applies softmax:R^n→R^n. The hard branch sets alpha_j=1_{j=j_*}, where j_* is the smallest maximizing index.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These are exactly the two alternative rules in the first Definition paragraph, restated with aliases in Remarks. The finite nonempty index set guarantees a maximizer and a unique smallest maximizing index; the fork is explicitly alternative, not simultaneous.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Both rules feed b_{i,k,h}=sum_{j=1}^n alpha_j V_{k,h}(y_j^{(k-1)}).
diagram_math_checks.justification: This is the first equality of the original displayed update; the incoming values arrow carries an n-tuple in (R^d)^n, so the weighted sum is in R^d.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The downward all-heads edge and previous-state edge feed F_k(y_i^{(k-1)},b_{i,k,1},...,b_{i,k,H}), producing y_i^{(k)}.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The caption states that the h-indexed computation is repeated for all H heads. F_k:(R^d)^{H+1}→R^d is defined at line 27 and the output is exactly the second equality at line 30. All nine arrows point from inputs to subsequent data; no commutativity, masking, or extra map constraint is asserted.
